svg.title: Act 130 of 2005: three statutory provisions crossed out
svg.desc: Original Final Vestige Studios documentary evidence diagram. The enrolled Louisiana Act 130 of 2005 struck out a former structured-settlement requirement to finish revenue and interest payments by July 1, 2009; a March 1 annual report to legislative natural-resources committees identifying transferred property and amounts paid; and a general direction to escrow disputed-property revenues pending a final court ruling. The diagram does not claim that the December 2000 consent judgment was canceled, that an existing court escrow was released, or that individual claimants did or did not receive payments.
svg.metadata: Creator: Final Vestige Studios editorial research team (AI-assisted production, human-editorial release required). Created: 2026-11-16. Title: Three instructions crossed out. Medium: original source-grounded vector diagram, not a historical facsimile, archival photograph, or AI-generated reconstruction. License: Copyright 2026 Final Vestige Studios; reuse requires permission. Primary legal source: Louisiana Legislature, enrolled Act No. 130 of 2005 (SB 210), printed page 4 (PDF zero-based index 3), https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=317802 Cross-check: Louisiana Legislature, Legislative Digest of Act No. 130, pages 1-2, https://www.legis.la.gov/Legis/ViewDocument.aspx?d=315214 Credit: Original diagram © Final Vestige Studios. Dates are statutory text, not observed payment dates. Alt text: An original three-panel diagram showing the 2005 Louisiana law's deletion of a July 1, 2009 structured-settlement deadline, a yearly March 1 report on land and payments, and an escrow rule for revenue from disputed property. Caption: Act 130's enrolled text crossed out three separate provisions about the Bohemia Spillway's statutory return process. This shows legislative deletions, not a canceled court judgment or proof of actual payments. Source: Louisiana Legislature, Act 130 (2005), p. 4, and official legislative digest, pp. 1-2.
